notes: BLOCKED before any menu or gameplay is reachable. 1830.EXE (Avalon Hill's 1993 railroad stock-market sim) hard-fails its own startup memory check every launch with 'You must have at least 2700K of expanded memory.' (exact string extracted from the EXE), then returns straight to the DOS prompt; the AUTOEXEC :loop re-launches it, so the guest cycles boot->fail->reboot indefinitely -- both 120s deep runs end with CS:IP=FFFF:1998 and 'boot: still in the BIOS (no boot, or read error)', i.e. the machine warm-reboots itself out of the crash rather than idling at a DOS prompt, and neither run produced a completed end-frame.ppm raster ('presented: none'). This is NOT a fixable schedule problem: the identical message, with the identical literal '2700K', appears in FOUR different configurations tried -- (1) default CONFIG.SYS with TOKAEMM.SYS loaded (RAM/EMS-on, the runner's default), (2) -NoEmm (no EMM driver at all), (3) --memory-mib 16 instead of the default 64, and (4) --interpreter instead of the native/JIT path -- so this is not a JIT-vs-interpreter divergence, not a total-RAM sizing issue (checked up to the emulator's --memory-mib ceiling of 64), and not something -ConfigExtra can route around. TOKAEMM's own arena math (crates/izarravm-firmware/roms/dos/tokaemm.asm) sizes the shared XMS/EMS/VCPI pool from installed RAM and should offer ~63 MB (thousands of 16K EMS pages) at a 64 MiB guest, far more than 2700K, and INT 67h AH=40h/41h/46h all answer as a healthy, framed, LIM-4.0-versioned manager -- so the driver reports itself present and 4.0-compliant, yet 1830 still measures zero usable expanded memory (identical outcome with EMS fully disabled). No DOS diagnostic tool was available in Toka-DOS's C:\DOS (no MEM.EXE, no DEBUG.COM) to trace the guest's actual INT 67h call sequence and pin down whether 1830 uses a nonstandard detection path (e.g. an IOCTL open of the 'EMMXXXX0' device rather than raw INT 67h) that TOKAEMM does not answer. Recommend a follow-up with real INT 67h call tracing before touching TOKAEMM code. The copy-protection bypass documented in ReadMe.txt (press ENTER at a manual word-lookup prompt after the first stock round) was never reached. Entry embeds TOKAMOUS.COM ahead of 1830.EXE for when/if this unblocks, since the game's stock-round and operating-round screens are described as mouse-driven menus; SOUND.EXE was not run since the crash predates any sound setup prompt. 486 chosen as the correct persona (1993 real-mode DOS title, no protected-mode/3D requirement).
